title: Color constancy and monocular depth: first controlled pilot
thesis_title: Design and Implementation of a Color-Constancy-Assisted Monocular Depth Estimation System

dataset.dataset: NYU Depth V2 labeled dataset (original authors' .mat)
dataset.selection: Random scenes without replacement from official split; one random frame per scene. Development selected before evaluation using one NumPy PCG64 generator.
dataset.depth_reference: depths field: Kinect-derived, projected and inpainted by original dataset authors; not model predictions
dataset.evaluation_warning: Small pilot subset, not the full 654-image benchmark. Inpainted depth is not a dense direct sensor measurement. No model is trained here.
dataset.validity: Finite reference depth >0 and <=10 meters within fixed crop. No depth scaling or predictions used in sample selection.

protocol.model: Depth Anything V2 Metric Hypersim Small

crop.description: rows45:471,columns41:601; scaled proportionally for other dimensions

protocol.aggregation: Arithmetic mean of per-image metrics; six casts equally weighted
protocol.transform: sRGB to linear RGB; diagonal channel gains; preserve mean luminance before clipping; clip; return to sRGB
protocol.half_strength: Square root of Gray-World gains (log-gain strength0.5); fixed before evaluation
protocol.quantization: Model receives RGB-to-BGR uint8 images after transformation
protocol.selection: Fixed methods and gains; no method parameters fitted to evaluation ground truth

limitations: Small deterministic pilot subset, not a full NYU benchmark reproduction
Synthetic global color casts do not reproduce all real illumination, camera processing, or spatially mixed lighting
Reference depth includes dataset preprocessing and sensor limitations
One pretrained model, no network training and no established novel algorithm contribution
Per-image bootstrap does not establish generalization to all scenes or datasets
